title: Retries, poison events, and the ordering tradeoff
outcome: Choose blocking retry, retry topics, or quarantine from the required per-entity behavior.
useCase: A consumer that must remain correct during outages and bad input.
benefits: Explicit recovery instead of infinite or silent failure.
drawbacks: Progress, ordering, and completeness can trade off.
version: Kafka 4.1 KRaft · lab Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 · legacy Rails adaptation notes
cue: Every retry design is also an ordering design.

trace.title: Classify failure
trace.detail: A transient outage and an invalid schema are different failures. Retrying malformed data forever does not repair it. Classify failures, bound attempts/delay, and retain enough safe context for diagnosis.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Receive A1 → fails → choose policy → observe whether A2/B1 may proceed → repair → redrive A1 → verify entity/projection version. Draw the order after every proposed retry design.

Use event_id, key, schema version, topic/partition/offset, attempt, and safe error category in diagnostics. Keep sensitive payloads out of logs.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Retry topics can break per-key ordering if not designed for it. A DLQ can become a graveyard. More workers do not solve a deterministic poison message.
